Senses.PreferredTarget: the Han hound chases the clod
AlternateTargets: a Han hound pursuing a dirt clod
the Han-family hound runs after the clod
Senses.Explanation: Literally, "the Han hound chases the clod." The phrase occurs 64 times in 46 allowlisted texts. A Blue Cliff Record comment gives the named allusion: the hound of the Han family was a swift dog, capable of tracking the cunning hare of Zhongshan; the monk in Dongshan's cold-and-heat exchange is compared to that hound running up the steps after a reflected moon and finding no moon there. Across the corpus the compact phrase is repeatedly contrasted with "the lion bites the person" (師子咬人，韓獹逐塊): one address says, "you must have the lion bite the person; do not imitate the Han hound chasing the clod" (直須師子咬人，莫學韓獹逐塊). It also occurs as a verdict after answers in public exchanges and as a verse line on Zhaozhou's attendant case. Zen bends the old hunting-dog allusion into a stock contrast between the person and the thrown clod, but the entry goes no farther than the corpus's own lion/person and hound/clod pairing.
Senses.Note: The graph translated as "hound" (獹) names the famed dog in the corpus's own allusion, and the graph translated as "Han" (韓) identifies it as the hound of the Han family. One allusive sense covers the simile, verdict, verse, and contrast. The variant "lion bites the person" uses both bite graphs (咬 and 齩) in witnesses.

Occurrences.Kwic: 其僧一似韓獹逐塊。連忙上階。捉其月影相似。又問。如何是無寒暑處。山云。寒時寒殺闍黎。熱時熱殺闍黎。如韓獹逐塊走到階上。又却不見月影。韓獹乃出戰國策。云韓氏之獹駿狗也。中山之兔狡兔也。是其獹方能尋其兔。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Blue Cliff Record of Chan Master Foguo Yuanwu (佛果圜悟禪師碧巖錄). Yuanwu Keqin compares the unnamed monk to the Han hound chasing a reflected moon and then explains the hound-and-rabbit allusion from the Strategies of the Warring States.
